_why: Feature discovery is two surfaces over one ledger: a 'what changed' card shown once per release family, and an optional spotlight walkthrough. These vectors pin the observable rules so a refactor cannot silently regress them: the two KV row names and the localStorage mirror name, the ledger's accumulative-array shape, release-family normalization and ordering, the announcement decision (first install records a baseline, an upgrade announces the window, a patch stays quiet), and the tour markers and their start gates. Both KV rows must also stay out of SessionConfiguration staleness: acknowledging a hint happens while the user is looking at a new feature, so it may never rebuild a live session (pinned separately by tests/session-wire.test.ts).

storage._mirrorHoldsLedgerOnly: the announcement window derives from the baseline row, so a mirror that also cached the window would announce a release the user has already seen until the KV read landed

parse._why: the stored row is a JSON string
an already-decoded array is accepted too
non-strings are dropped, empty strings are dropped
a corrupt row degrades to an empty ledger rather than blocking boot
an object is not a ledger
an empty string is an empty ledger

append._why: re-acknowledging is a no-op and must not grow the row

ledger._unionWhy: The row is overwritten whole because settings.db KV has no append, so two windows acknowledging different features inside one round trip would let the later write clobber the earlier one and lose an acknowledgement the user already made. Union is correct here ONLY because the ledger is append-only: no code path removes an id, so merging cannot revive anything. A ledger that gained a 'forget this hint' action would need a tombstone instead.

union._why: a concurrent acknowledgement from another window survives our write
base order is preserved and only the new id is appended
an identical ledger is a no-op
merging with nothing returns the base unchanged
merging into nothing returns the other side
a tour completion marker is an id like any other and unions the same way
empty ids from a corrupt row are dropped

cases._why: a first install records the baseline and announces the family it shipped in, so the introducing release is not permanently invisible
a first install on a family with nothing in the registry records a baseline and stays quiet
a patch release inside the announced family does not re-announce
a downgrade does not re-announce either
an upgrade announces the window, and a feature shipped before the baseline never resurfaces
skipping two releases catches up on both, and 0.10 sorts above 0.9
an unparseable running version cannot be decided, so nothing is written and nothing shows
evergreen hints are not tied to a release and never enter an announcement window

isDone._why: arriving at the feature is not the same as finishing its walkthrough

mayStart._why: This answers 'is anything else holding the screen'. Whether THIS arrival is eligible at all is startsTourOnArrival below, which needs the previous verdict and therefore lives with the sweep that has it.

cases._why: nothing else on screen: the walkthrough may start
the card outranks the walkthrough
only one walkthrough runs at a time
a completed walkthrough never replays
a skipped walkthrough counts as declined and never replays
an entry with no steps has nothing to start

startsOnArrival._why: Only a false→true transition starts a walkthrough. This is the rule that keeps two interruptions from happening: a surface already open at boot (restored window state, a deep link) is acknowledged rather than greeted with a modal over the first frame, and a tour deferred because the card was up does not fire later on some unrelated mutation while the user is still sitting on that page — the card already told them about it.

cases._why: the user just navigated here: this is an arrival
the first sweep records what is already open without starting anything
still sitting on a page already acknowledged is not a new arrival
leaving a surface starts nothing
leaving and already-gone both start nothing
an entry never evaluated before is treated as the first sweep's job

parse._why: a mirror written by an older shape still yields its ledger
corrupt mirror degrades to null, which means 'paint nothing yet'
